transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been kind of arranging my days around avoiding elevators. Like, I’ll take five flights of stairs at my apartment instead, which sounds healthy, I guess—my friend joked I’m getting free cardio—but it’s not really the point.

And work-wise, I train people on computer stuff, and I actually turned down a workshop because it was in a high-rise. I felt stupid doing that. I also stopped visiting one of my older computer students because his building doesn’t really have another option besides the elevator, and… I don’t know, it’s starting to mess with things.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or uncomfortable in social situations, especially where you might be observed or evaluated by others?

Um… social situations? I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I train people for work, so I’m kind of used to being watched while I explain things—though sometimes people ask the same computer question three different ways and I start wondering if I’m explaining it badly. But that’s more annoying than scary, I guess.

I haven’t really noticed being anxious because people are judging me or anything like that. At least, that’s not the main thing I’m thinking about.
When you’re in or think about taking an elevator, do you feel intense anxiety, panic, or fear that something bad will happen, like getting trapped or running out of air?

Yeah… I mean, I know logically elevators in an office building are probably safe. Like, people use them all day and don’t think twice about it.

But when I’m actually standing there looking at the doors—especially the older ones in my apartment building, or at work—my brain just kind of goes, “Nope.” It feels like I’m about to get stuck in there, or like it could drop or something. And I know that sounds dramatic, because obviously I’m not an elevator mechanic or anything, but it just feels really real in the moment.
Do you experience similar anxiety or avoidance in situations other than elevators, such as crowded places, open spaces, or other specific scenarios?

Um… I don’t think so. Not that I’ve really noticed, anyway.

Like, crowded places can be annoying, sure—like when you’re trying to get through a grocery store and somebody parks their cart sideways in the aisle, which somehow happens every single time—but I don’t think I’m scared in those situations. And open spaces… no, I don’t think that’s a thing for me.

It’s mainly the elevator part that sticks out. I mean, unless I’m missing something you mean by “specific scenarios,” but nothing else is coming to mind.
When you're faced with taking an elevator, do you ever feel physical symptoms like your heart racing, sweating, or feeling like you can't breathe?

Yeah, definitely. It’s weird because it can happen before I’m even fully in one. Like if I step toward the elevator and hear it kind of clunk open, my chest tightens up right away, and my hands get sweaty.

And then I get this quick rush of panic, like my body reacts before my brain has even really caught up. Which is annoying, because I’ll be standing there thinking, “Okay, you’re just trying to go up a few floors,” but my body is already acting like something bad is happening.
How long have you felt this way about elevators? Did this fear start suddenly, or has it been building up over time?

Um… it’s been about seven months, I think. Around then.

It wasn’t like I was always thrilled about elevators before, but it got noticeable shortly after I moved into this fifth-floor apartment. Which, you know, at first I was like, “Great, decent view, less street noise,” and then of course the elevator becomes the thing I have to deal with every day.

There was this scare with it not long after I moved in, and after that it kind of stuck. So I guess it started pretty suddenly after that, but then it’s been building into more of a habit over the months.
Have you ever had a sudden episode of intense fear or discomfort that came out of the blue, without a clear trigger or specific situation involved?

Out of the blue? Um… I don’t think so, not really.

I mean, I’ve had moments where I’m stressed and then my brain kind of spirals, like if I’m late for work or I forgot to send a training document—my job has a million little moving parts, and somehow the one email you miss is always the one someone asks about—but that feels different. There’s usually a reason.

So, no, I can’t think of a time where it just hit me randomly with no trigger or situation attached.
Have you ever found yourself worrying a lot about having another panic attack or feeling that rush of fear again, even when you’re not actually in an elevator or facing the situation?

Um… I don’t know if I’d say I worry a lot about that specifically. Like, I’m not sitting at my desk thinking, “What if I panic later?” all day or anything.

Sometimes it crosses my mind if I know I’m going somewhere with an elevator, but then I’ll get distracted by work stuff or whatever else is going on. Honestly, my job already has enough little things to keep track of—trainings, calendars, people rescheduling at the last second—so my brain is usually busy with that until I’m actually near the elevator. Then it kind of hits me more.
Do you ever feel anxious or worried about having another panic attack when you’re not actually in an elevator or near one?

Not really, no… I mean, if I’m not around an elevator, I’m usually thinking about other stuff. Work, mostly. Like today I was trying to fix this training signup thing that kept showing the wrong date, and that kind of ate up my whole brain for a while.

So… I don’t think I sit around worrying about having that rush of fear again. It’s more like it comes up when I know I’m about to deal with an elevator, or I’m near one. Otherwise it’s not really on my mind.
Have you ever had a sudden episode of intense fear or panic when you weren’t anywhere near an elevator or thinking about one?

No, I don’t think so. Like, if I’m nowhere near an elevator and it’s not even on my mind, I don’t really get that sudden panic feeling.

I mean, I get normal stress, like work stuff—someone changes a training room last minute and then three people email me like it’s an emergency—but that’s not the same thing. It’s not like this random wave of panic out of nowhere.
